summary: The grain leaving Luminara is bound for Fleet under a protective agreement, but Verge families worry that sending reserves away leaves their own community short; a mother and her son watch the risky convoy depart.
settingText: LUMINARA FIELDS — VERGE AGRICULTURAL FREIGHT DOCK — MORNING

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: LUMINARA FIELDS — MORNING

dialogueInline.speaker: Dock Worker
dialogueInline.text: Fleet's bought another three holds. We're loading the reserve bins now.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: Leave the local bins sealed. That's next month's ration.

dialogueInline.speaker: Boy
dialogueInline.text: If they're taking our grain, what do we eat when the next harvest's late?

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: What's left here. And whatever the convoy earns us. That's why everyone's arguing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Boy
dialogueInline.text: They say the Shards might take it before Fleet gets it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: They might. But keeping everything here won't feed the settlements waiting for it.

panelPlan: Broad establishing view of productive Luminara fields and a Verge grain dock: intact agricultural infrastructure, multiple sealed grain bins, workers, vehicle lanes and long tan-green modular freighters. Grain is unmistakable as bulk food, not ambiguous cargo.

Close on dock crews opening reserve bins and loading marked grain containers into a named visually trackable freighter. A worker tells another how many holds Fleet has purchased while the mother, involved in dock logistics, guards the allocation for Luminara households.

The boy has overheard anxious workers discussing export, Fleet protection and Shard seizures; he asks about their own food while watching the grain move. The mother gives a practical incomplete answer, not a promise from an unseen state.

Freighters detach from the dock along a defined cleared departure lane; any visible thrust or field maneuver occurs away from exposed people. Their orientation and the distinctive lead freighter's shape remain consistent.
Final smaller close view of mother and son watching the convoy shrink beyond the farms. The mother's uncertain expression carries the risk; do not insert narration or symbolic slogans.
directionInline: Begin with a shared material stake, not faction theory. Both the Core-bound buyers and Verge residents need the grain; losing it harms both and may also starve Shard communities that normally seize portions of passing commerce.
The mother and boy remain on Luminara for this departure scene. Their later presence aboard an attacked transport requires an explicit, believable boarding/transfer explanation, not a silent jump.

Maintain consistent physical freight dimensions and safe departure clearance. All dialogue belongs to specific visible speakers; the dock worker is an unnamed speaking extra, not a new recurring character.

summary: The grain convoy enters the slow, debris-filled Kaldr passage; Naomi's escort must accept Thunderbreak's protection despite Verge mistrust of the Fleet's growing authority over routes.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: KALDR RIFT — CERTIFIED PASSAGE

dialogueInline.speaker: Second
dialogueInline.text: Drift markers moved again. The cleared lane's two freighters wide.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Put the heaviest grain ship in front. Nothing overtakes inside the wreck field.

dialogueInline.speaker: Second
dialogueInline.text: Thunderbreak's asking to close on our port flank.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Give them the approach. We don't give them our navigation authority.

panelPlan: Wide look at a physically dangerous wreckage field: slowly drifting asteroids, fractured old hulls and navigational beacons or clean graphics identifying a narrow surveyed corridor. No luminous magical tube.

Identify the distinct grain freighter from Luminara, with escorted cargo modules and several smaller ships maintaining clearance. This is a low-relative-speed volume after field transit, not faster-than-light obstacle dodging.
Within Naomi's established tan-green practical cockpit, Second compares real drift markers while Naomi adjusts convoy spacing with physical controls.
Blue-gold Thunderbreak enters the edge of formation in a consistent direction and at a scale well larger than escorts yet separated by sensible maneuvering distance.
Close on Naomi assessing the new Fleet position, not a generic glare; the final image reveals an unrecognized compact contact tucked against wreck cover or an obscured approach vector.
directionInline: Fleet escorts are militarily powerful; Verge pilots retain local route knowledge and want to control their own traffic. This is a conflict of jurisdiction and need, not mere dislike.
Keep trackable positions for lead freighter, escorts, Thunderbreak, wreck mass and possible incoming raiders. Debris has drift and requires continuous survey.
No unexplained labels on cockpit screens or background hulls.

summary: Naomi spots evidence of a planned cargo interception: the Shards know the convoy's exact route. She holds formation while Fleet screens the threatened grain freighter.

dialogueInline.speaker: Second
dialogueInline.text: Small hulls behind the breaker. They're pacing the grain ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: They're already inside the lane? Someone gave them the crossing window.

dialogueInline.speaker: Second
dialogueInline.text: Fleet wants us to fall behind Thunderbreak.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Tell them we know this approach. I'll take the freighter through; they can cover the flank.

dialogueInline.speaker: Second
dialogueInline.text: Two contacts accelerating. They're not after the escort.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Warn the cargo master. Seal the holds now.

panelPlan: Opening widescreen cockpit-view panel establishes the geometry already seen: compact raider contacts aligned against the identifiable grain freighter, with Thunderbreak protecting the convoy's open flank.

Naomi and Second compare drift and encounter timing at real working consoles. Her braid and brow scar match her approved identity; the second officer is visibly distinct and contributes decisions rather than asking rhetorical questions.
Close inserts reveal maneuver markers instead of predictive essays: two raider vectors converging on a freighter's service/docking fittings.
Naomi gives a rapid warning and continues actually piloting. Second passes the seal order through a functional transmitter while the convoy changes speed in response.
End on exterior: Shard cutters emerge from wreck cover toward the grain freighter's cargo holds; Fleet reacts but cannot be everywhere along the narrow path.
directionInline: Nobody yet knows which individual supplied the raiders with the crossing window; Naomi infers only that the raid was informed.
Keep Venn's cruiser a protective presence, not a vessel that can instantaneously teleport between freighters.
Dialogue must reflect flight decisions and a developing situation. Avoid abstract confidence or thematic self-repetition.

summary: The Triarch's standing grain-seizure policy becomes a physical fight: Abby coordinates a limited cargo grab, Billie presses the interception harder, and Venn uses a derelict's mass to protect the freighter at a real cost to Thunderbreak.
settingText: KALDR RIFT — CONVOY INTERCEPTION / THUNDERBREAK COMMAND

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: Two cutters on the grain ship. They're lining up with the transfer collars.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: If we clear the wreck, we're exposing the freighter's starboard hold.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Bring our bow along the derelict. Push it across their approach. Keep the grain ship in our lee.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: We'll scrape the port armor.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Log the section. Execute the turn.

panelPlan: Start in coherent exterior wide view, preserving convoy geometry: two Shard cargo cutters moving toward the grain ship's collars; a large drifting derelict sits between Thunderbreak and an exposed approach.
On Thunderbreak's broad older blue-gold bridge, tactical reports a cargo interception, not an unexplained passenger massacre. Venn hears an officer's specific collision/damage warning.

Compact inset map or exterior insert shows Venn's proposed motion: Thunderbreak moves beside and contacts the derelict at low relative speed using its reinforced forward shield/armor, transferring momentum to obstruct the cutters' line. No spectacular head-on high-speed crash.

A dominant exterior panel tracks the derelict sliding across the raiders' approach as Thunderbreak incurs a visible scrape/damage on the port bow armor. Sparks and debris are local to contact, not an impossible ship-wide explosion.

A Shard cutter breaks away to avoid collision; another continues along the grain hull. In the last narrow panel an engineer or status visual confirms the same port-bow panel damaged and maneuvering margin reduced.
directionInline: Abby and Billie are both executing a Triarch standing order to seize grain from moving trade. Their distinct tactical attitudes should read in external action, not a premature ideological speech; if no Shard command interior is shown, do not invent their dialogue on this page.
Preserve named vessel hull silhouettes and the port-bow damage through the remainder of this issue and into subsequent continuity when relevant.
Respect mass, relative velocity, contact location, and follow-through. The derelict's new course physically changes the defensive geometry, and there is a cost.

summary: A grain freighter's service collar is breached during the Shard boarding action; civilian passengers waiting for onward transfer shelter while an already-embarked security detail protects them, and the mother seals her son's emergency gear.
settingText: GRAIN FREIGHTER — ACCESS COMPARTMENT BESIDE CARGO HOLD

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: GRAIN FREIGHTER — PASSENGER ACCESS

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: Keep still. I need the helmet seal closed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Boy
dialogueInline.text: Are they taking the grain?

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: I don't know. Stay behind this door.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raider
dialogueInline.text: Cargo hold only. Leave the passengers.

dialogueInline.speaker: Fleet Sergeant
dialogueInline.text: Passenger section's sealed. Get clear of the cargo hatch.

panelPlan: Establish why mother and boy are aboard: a brief practical boarding/context panel shows them serving as registered family-passengers for a planned onward relief transfer at Auric, having moved from the Luminara dock to the freighter before departure. If this conflicts with their already-established dock departure, revise their first-page blocking so they board before the convoy lifts rather than teleporting between locations.

Clear cross-section spatial logic: one freight access/collar, grain stacks and secured cargo hatches, a distinct passenger access alcove, emergency pressure door and the Fleet security detail already stationed with the convoy's protected passengers.

A Shard boarding cutter attaches at the cargo collar; local cutting and a short pressure leak disturb straps and loose cloth. Do not depict endless decompression, uncontrolled zero gravity or randomly flying bodies.
At ground-level human scale, the mother seats the boy in an emergency helmet and checks the neck seal while shielding him with her own body. He stays a protected civilian, not a combat actor.

A raider orders a crew member toward cargo, while a Fleet sergeant on the freighter's pre-embarked security detail directs civilians behind the sealed passenger door. Maintain distinguishable adult uniforms and grounded poses.
End with an external view or pressure-seal indicator showing that the passenger door holds while the grain holds remain contested; the family is not presented as magically evacuated.
directionInline: Passenger presence, security pre-positioning and compartment topology must be established before contact. Do not imply Fleet troops arrived through an unexplained teleport or docking event.

The child's fear concerns the family grain and immediate danger; adults respond with task-specific dialogue. The Shard raider acts under cargo-seizure orders, while potential collateral danger remains a genuine consequence of the attack.
No visible injury to the child. No gravity or suction spectacle unsupported by this compartment's pressure state.

summary: With one Shard cutter escaping through the debris, Venn declines an easy pursuit shot in order to keep the convoy protected; Naomi and the freighter crew extract survivors while the destroyed and spilled grain reduces everyone's eventual share.
settingText: THUNDERBREAK COMMAND / KALDR RIFT — CONVOY AFTERMATH

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: One cutter's getting clear. We have a firing window if we leave the freighter's flank.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Stay with the freighter. Put the reserve shield over its damaged hold.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: That cutter will be out of range in forty seconds.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: I know. Give Naomi the pressure-safe approach.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Passenger seal's holding. Grain is venting from the split container. I'll take the survivors to Auric.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: I'll escort what's left.

panelPlan: Exterior establishes two concurrent facts: one raider cutter escaping behind moving wreckage, while the identifiable grain freighter has a damaged grain container and local hull/pallet damage from boarding action. Grain grains and cargo fragments drift into space in quantities appropriate to the breach.
On Thunderbreak command, an officer offers a credible short firing window, but doing so would move defensive coverage off the grain ship; the choice has an observable spatial cost.
Venn refuses pursuit with a practical protective order and assigns the surviving passengers and compromised cargo to a safer path.

Naomi's smaller escort maneuvers beside the compromised freighter; an operational check confirms the passenger pressure seal still holds. The mother and boy remain in the passenger section; no impossible second evacuation is depicted.

Show a believable aftermath assessment: intact containers continue under escort, some grain is lost to space or fire and some may have been taken by raiders. Distinguish captured, destroyed and surviving cargo rather than treating all as 'lost'.

Final wide image shows diminished but moving convoy in certified passage, Thunderbreak's damaged port bow plainly visible, and the attacking cutter's diminishing engine trace. Victory is partial and no triumphant pose replaces the civilian loss.
directionInline: Record that the raid's aggregate outcome leaves less grain for Verge, Fleet and Shards; nobody obtains an unlimited reward from a damaged trade system. No invented precise casualty totals or cargo tonnages.

Venn's first choice spent cruiser armor to block the attackers; her second choice preserves civilian protection but permits a raider to escape. Those are distinct decisions with distinct consequences.
Fleet personnel and Naomi only know what their instruments or observed events support. The identity of the route-information source remains unknown to them.

summary: The protected convoy reaches Auric with damaged grain holds and frightened survivors. An improvised, secular remembrance of the dead cannot obscure the logistical consequences of the raid.
settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — ARRIVAL BERTH AND CASUALTY STATION — EVENING

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: AURIC BAZAAR — EVENING

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Two grain holds intact. One ruptured. The rest of the cargo's being counted at berth.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: The family next to us didn't make it off their ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Tell the dock registrar their names. I'll make sure our security report includes them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Boy
dialogueInline.text: Is our grain coming back?

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: Not all of it.

panelPlan: Wide cargo-berth arrival showing the same long freighter and smaller surviving escorts docking with clear geometry. Thunderbreak remains beyond the berths with its damaged port bow, not pristine or docked in an impossibly small berth.

Verge port workers unload intact grain containers beside split and smoke-marked cargo. A practical counting station records the remaining grain using abstract graphical counts without invented readable display labels.

Medics and workers escort passengers from the access compartment along a visibly connected gangway. The mother and boy wear the same clothing and emergency gear state as at the attack; his helmet is removed only once pressure-safe.

One modest remembrance beat: civilians acknowledge missing people beside a casualty list managed by a registrar. Venn is present briefly, listening to the mother's specific loss rather than conducting an ornate ceremony.

Close on the boy watching grain unloaded into separate allocations and asking a direct question; his mother cannot promise the cargo will return. End on the visible gap in the cargo lineup, not a motto.
directionInline: Do not move the scene to a grand memorial hall. Place remembrance in the material aftermath, allowing civilians to express grief in their own way.
No casualty names or memorial inscriptions appear unless explicitly scripted. No omniscient tally or invented number; loss is evident in remaining holds and mourning.
Keep the rescue successful but incomplete. The mother's earlier concern about exported grain now has a tangible, personal answer.

summary: Auric must allocate diminished grain between local households, standing commitments and Fleet deliveries. Halev faces residents and arriving survivors while Naomi refuses to mistake Fleet protection for political consent.
settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — PUBLIC GRAIN BERTH / CIVIC DESK — NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: The ship arrived with less grain than the manifests promised. Our local bins won't cover every delivery.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: Fleet's contract takes its share before the market opens. People here have already paid for the rest.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Fleet protected the convoy. That doesn't give them a vote on Auric's remaining food.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Then Auric makes the allocations. Keep the families out of the loading lane until we can count it properly.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: My son heard us arguing at Luminara. What am I supposed to tell him now?

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Tell him I'll have the household allotments posted before the next shift. I won't promise what I haven't counted.

panelPlan: Market and dock in working night light: lined-up freighter containers, sheltered families, recognizable local grain bins and visible Verge cargo crews; the location feels capable and inhabited rather than ruined.

Halev works at the berth desk with damaged physical manifests while Wallace calculates the commercial impact. Naomi arrives in the same practical gear as the cockpit pages, without changing into Fleet uniform.
Naomi challenges the idea that Fleet's rescue grants it authority over Verge food; this is a specific allocation issue, not a speech about sovereignty.
The mother and boy are among individual residents awaiting distribution, not anonymous suffering background. Their family question interrupts an argument with a concrete need.
Halev chooses a local inventory and household-allocation process, an authority Auric actually possesses. End with workers separating intact grain from compromised stock.
directionInline: Fleet wants supply and connection; Auric has its own political institutions. Both benefit from the route yet disagree over who controls its consequences.
Do not reduce Wallace to a comic-relief cynic. His contract and price concerns are legitimate, even where they conflict with humanitarian priorities.
Any ledger or interface may show simple abstract figures, but no unscripted words or numbers.

summary: Jex Marrin privately meets Billie over the information that made a limited Shard grain interception possible; he discovers the raid damaged the cargo and tells her that killing trade will starve the same Shard families he hoped to help.
settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — TRADE CORRIDOR / DOCK-SIDE BROKER TABLE

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: You had the grain route. Transfer windows, escort positions, the lot. Why did the hold split?

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Fleet shoved half a wreck between us and the freighter. We had seconds to get clear.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Now half the cargo's no use to anyone. That grain was meant to feed people on both sides.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Your buyers still have their ports. Our families get what we bring home.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: I gave you a way to take containers, not wreck a ship full of people.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Then give us a better way to make Fleet notice. We don't get one by asking.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: I'll keep looking. I'm not selling you another passenger's life.

panelPlan: Quiet but busy side of the Auric market, not a secret mystical chamber: Jex checks an actual route slate and cargo balance while dock labor continues through the background.
Billie appears with her distinctive vivid-red hair and pale-gray/red Shard flight layers; she is human and angry, not gleefully manic or glamour-posed.

Short physical insert shows Jex's original route token or exchange key being returned or handled by Billie. The device contains crossing information and limited cargo-transfer windows, not mystical power.

Jex compares expected intact grain transfer with the ruined cargo observed at the dock. Billie disputes the premise that Fleet will ever distribute resources fairly, speaking from Shard deprivation rather than cartoon sadism.

Conversation ends without reconciliation. Billie departs toward an established small Shard transport connected to Ashfang's operations; Jex stays to renegotiate surviving cargo. Neither knows future events.
directionInline: Jex is an idealistic opportunist who knowingly helps grain reach Shard people through controlled seizures while also profiting from trade. He does not endorse passenger harm. His dual dealings are politically dangerous to him and others.

Billie and Abby carried out the Triarch's existing raiding order; the raid was not invented by Jex. Jex supplied crossing intelligence with expectations he could not enforce. Billie has real historical grievances and may interpret the damage as proof of Fleet aggression.
Do not have Jex confess to Verge officials or Fleet, since they do not yet know his role. Do not assign mystical language or vague remarks about 'flow'.

summary: At Black Drift, captured grain arrives alongside a damaged Ashfang Marauder. Repairs and food distribution reveal that Shard raids require ongoing trade and that this interception brought less food than hoped.
settingText: BLACK DRIFT — SHARD REPAIR YARD — FOLLOWING SHIFT

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: BLACK DRIFT — FOLLOWING SHIFT

dialogueInline.speaker: Tessa
dialogueInline.text: Ashfang's port collar is torn through. We can patch it, but not before the next shift.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Unload the grain first. Families are waiting at the ration point.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: We got three containers past Thunderbreak.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tessa
dialogueInline.text: And lost the others when the hold broke. That wasn't all Fleet's doing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Three containers won't last. We need merchants willing to make the next crossing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: You want them willing. I want them unable to ignore us.

panelPlan: Exterior of Black Drift, a working inhabited Shard industrial settlement. The angular, named Ashfang Marauder matches its approved hull precisely, with a visibly damaged docking/cargo collar matching the attack and approach.

Large human-scale panel of workers welding the collar while other workers remove three surviving sealed grain containers. Children or other civilians may wait at distribution points but never enter dangerous machinery or combat.

Tessa in compact flight clothing and silver-gray curls inspects the collar and predicts limited repair time; Abby tall, Black, braided and still, directs grain to ration crews rather than posing above them.
Billie reports her tactical success with energy and anger. Tessa ties material loss to the damaged hold without portraying herself as an uninvolved moral judge; she participated in Shard command.
End with Abby and Billie holding different priorities in a work bay: upcoming trade crossings versus forcing Fleet attention. Neither declares a final split.
directionInline: Shard repair yards are competent, maintained, lived-in industrial spaces; workers and civilians have individual lives. Never use skulls, spikes or barbarian raider cues.
Grain received by the Shards does not erase losses to all sides. Abby and Billie both resent the need to raid, but their preferred future paths differ.
Abby and Tessa are sisters; preserve the established distinct visual identities and let shared familiarity inform their reactions without turning the page into explanatory genealogy.

summary: Abby resolves a dock-worker dispute over distributing captured grain and repairs through authority and expertise, rather than physical humiliation; Billie objects to spending scarce time on logistics while Tessa knows the cost of a failed seal.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dock Worker
dialogueInline.text: The ration crew wants the last container now. If we stop repairs, Ashfang misses the convoy after next.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Use the cargo lift while the weld cools. Keep the pressure frame braced until Tessa signs it off.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tessa
dialogueInline.text: That frame goes back under load too soon, the collar tears open again.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Another crossing means another Fleet ship between us and dinner.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Then we need the collar intact and enough grain left for people who can't board a cutter.

panelPlan: Abby's authority is visible amid labor: cargo lift, mechanical braces, pressure-frame repair and waiting ration workers occupy coherent positions in the hangar.
A frustrated adult dock worker argues over which task has priority, with a real concern about the next potential food delivery.

Abby reassigns lift work and directs the repair sequence so ration distribution and structural repair can continue without needless risk. Crew act on her precise instructions because she understands the work and their needs.
Tessa tests the braced collar and challenges premature release; she and Abby exchange an experienced sibling glance or abbreviated response grounded in shared practical history.
Billie objects to the necessity of another dangerous seizure. Her anger at ongoing scarcity is visible in how she watches hungry people receive small shares.
Conclude with a working lift delivering grain to the ration point while Ashfang's collar remains in repair; no wrestling, impossible throws or ceremonial slogan.
directionInline: The disagreement is among competent Shard adults under real pressure. Abby is not infallible and Billie is not a manic caricature.
An anonymous dock worker may speak without receiving an invented proper name. The physical repair and cargo movements must remain consistent panel to panel.
Billie's desire to make Fleet answer for historical harms should be shown through her focus on who imposes the shortages, not an abstract threat to civilians.

summary: Abby, Billie and Tessa review the raid with enough grain for immediate relief but none of the long-term security their people need. Abby begins to consider access to supplies without seizures; Billie believes forcing powerful outsiders to feel consequences may win more than permission.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: We came back with three containers. The next two convoys are delaying departure.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Fleet will call that a victory. They can afford to wait. We can't.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tessa
dialogueInline.text: Neither can the families who planned to eat from those ships.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: If merchants could deliver a set share to our settlements, we'd have ships free to do something besides chase grain.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Why would Fleet let them? They've watched us go hungry for generations.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: I don't know if they would. I know this route won't last if every shipment ends damaged.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Then they need to be afraid of what happens when they leave us out.

panelPlan: Functional Shard command table with physical grain-container tokens, actual transit lanes and a repair manifest. No ornamental infinite hologram, unscripted writing or ritual mapping.
Abby moves markers for captured grain and delayed merchant departures; the table makes clear how successful seizures can reduce future supply by discouraging trade.

Billie challenges the possibility of voluntary access while thinking of genuine inherited losses and Fleet indifference. Her anger is controlled enough to be credible, not an uncontrolled snarling pose.
Tessa handles repair/civilian impact data she is personally responsible for, reminding them that civilians on all sides bear the cost. Her complicity in Shard command remains intact.
Abby considers negotiated supplies as a possibility, not a sudden conversion or accomplished agreement. Billie believes coercion might force recognition as well as provide food.
End on unresolved differences and a summons/order signal from the Triarch, whose raiding standing order governs their work.
directionInline: No one says a maxim about 'flow', 'fire first' or 'living first'. Conversations respond to one another's concrete proposals and objections.

Abby and Billie both believe Shards should not have to raid to survive. Abby is beginning to imagine receiving supplies voluntarily; Billie sees punitive coercion as a route to supplies and historical reckoning.
Abby and Tessa's sister relationship and Billie's bond with Tessa underlie the disagreement without explicit family-history exposition.

summary: Abby stands before the Silent Triarch and receives three incompatible Shard imperatives from three distinct political authorities: raid, trade and fear.
settingText: SILENT TRIARCH CHAMBER — SHARD POWER CENTER

dialogueInline.speaker: Raid
dialogueInline.text: Strike to feed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Trade
dialogueInline.text: Flow sustains.

dialogueInline.speaker: Fear
dialogueInline.text: Terror binds.

panelPlan: Abby stands before three seated Triarch members in a dark but technologically practical Shard chamber; the three masks have distinct silhouettes and fixed left-center-right positions.
Close portrait of the jagged Raid mask delivering the order to strike to feed.
Close portrait of the pale etched Trade mask saying flow sustains.
Close portrait of the glossy dark Fear mask saying terror binds.
Final panel returns to Abby standing among the three competing authorities, making their political contradiction visible.
directionInline: RELEASED-CANON RECONSTRUCTION: This recipe was reverse-engineered from the final published Issue 1 page. Preserve the published story state, composition logic, causal action and exact readable text. Use current RexPrompt character names and handles for live identity; do not invent additional text or story information.
The Silent Triarch are political rulers, not supernatural beings. Preserve three distinct masks and positions. No ritual magic, runes, incense, sacred glow or mystic framing.

summary: At Auric, Halev turns the rescue into a list of unmet civilian needs; Wallace attacks Core-style tariffs and Naomi demands disciplined formations instead of raider-bought maps.
settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — WORKING MARKET AND CIVIC DOCK — DAY

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: We need more than food. Medicine. Fuel cells. Heat. Lights for the out-rings.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: And fewer tariffs dressed as blessings.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: You want safety? You ride in formation and you stop buying maps from raiders.

panelPlan: Wide market view keeps Halev, Wallace and Naomi in a working civilian environment surrounded by cargo, power hardware, merchants and families.
A child and caregiver sit beside a portable heater/power unit in the foreground, making Halev's list of needs physically visible.
Halev counts medicine, fuel cells, heat and lights on his fingers while speaking to Wallace and Naomi.
Wallace answers with the tariff complaint in a close portrait, skeptical rather than villainous.
Naomi steps into the argument and states the operational condition for safety: formation discipline and no raider maps.
directionInline: RELEASED-CANON RECONSTRUCTION: This recipe was reverse-engineered from the final published Issue 1 page. Preserve the published story state, composition logic, causal action and exact readable text. Use current RexPrompt character names and handles for live identity; do not invent additional text or story information.
Auric is a capable but resource-constrained Verge freeport. Civilians remain individuals with practical work and needs; do not render them as misery wallpaper.

summary: Wallace defends the price of working route information while Halev cuts the argument short and offers a narrow deal: essential cargo only, with Fleet on the wing if it accepts Verge terms.
